title: Running Sum with Array or Vector
description: Given an integer array, update it into its running-sum form. This is the kind of index-based traversal you should be comfortable doing in both Java arrays or ArrayLists and C++ vectors.
intendedApproachSummary: Traverse from left to right and add the previous accumulated value into the current position.
wrongApproachHints: Do not recompute each prefix from scratch.
hints: Each position should absorb the previous prefix sum.

examples.explanation: Each value becomes the sum of all values up to that index.

title: Count Vowels with String Traversal
description: Given a lowercase string s, return how many vowels it contains. This builds the habit of char-by-char traversal before heavier string and collection work.
inputFormat: A lowercase string s without spaces
outputFormat: Return the number of vowels in s
intendedApproachSummary: Scan the string once and count characters that belong to the vowel set.
wrongApproachHints: You do not need nested loops for each vowel.
hints: Check one character at a time.

examples.explanation: The vowels are e, u, a, i, and o.

title: Merge Strings Alternately
description: Merge two strings by alternating characters. This teaches StringBuilder or mutable-string habits that show up constantly in DSA implementations.
inputFormat: Two lowercase strings word1 and word2 without spaces
intendedApproachSummary: Use two indices and a builder-like result container that appends from each string while available.
wrongApproachHints: Do not stop at the shorter string.
Avoid repeated immutable concatenation in a long loop.
hints: Append from the first string, then the second.
Flush the remaining suffix at the end.

examples.explanation: Characters are taken alternately from each word.

functionContract.javaSignature: public String mergeAlternately(String first, String second)

title: Valid Anagram with Frequency Maps
description: Given two lowercase strings a and b, return true if b is an anagram of a. This is a clean first HashMap or unordered_map style frequency problem.
inputFormat: Two lowercase strings a and b without spaces
outputFormat: Return true if they are anagrams, else false
intendedApproachSummary: Count frequencies and compare them, or increment from one string and decrement from the other.
wrongApproachHints: Sorting works but the intended collections habit is frequency counting.
Different lengths can never be anagrams.
hints: Use a map or fixed-size frequency table.

examples.explanation: Both strings contain the same letters with the same frequencies.

functionContract.javaSignature: public boolean isAnagram(String first, String second)

title: Stack Query Simulator
description: Process push, pop, and top queries on a stack. This is about getting fluent with stack API usage before stack-based DSA patterns.
inputFormat: q lines of queries in the format 1 x, 2, or 3
outputFormat: For each type 3 query, print the current top or -1
intendedApproachSummary: Use push, pop, and peek semantics over a stack-like container without shifting data.
wrongApproachHints: Do not scan or shift the whole collection on each pop.
Check emptiness before reading the top.
hints: The most recently pushed element is the only candidate for top.

title: Queue Query Simulator
description: Process enqueue, dequeue, and front queries on a queue. This helps users stop using slow remove-from-front array habits and move to real queue APIs.
outputFormat: For each type 3 query, print the current front or -1
intendedApproachSummary: Use FIFO operations directly through a queue-like library container.
wrongApproachHints: Do not remove index 0 from a dynamic array repeatedly.
Front and rear are not interchangeable.
hints: Offer at the back and poll from the front.

providedTypes: queue operations encoded as query pairs

title: Remove Adjacent Duplicates
description: Repeatedly remove adjacent equal characters from a string until no such pair remains. This is a clean pattern for stack-backed cleanup using a mutable result structure.
inputFormat: A lowercase string s without spaces
outputFormat: Return the reduced string, or Empty if nothing remains
intendedApproachSummary: Treat the current answer as a stack: pop when the next character matches the top, otherwise push it.
wrongApproachHints: Repeated substring deletion is slower than intended.
A removal can create a new adjacent pair.
hints: Compare with the last kept character.
Think of the builder as a stack.

examples.explanation: bb is removed first, then aa is removed.

title: K Largest Elements with Heap
description: Given an array and integer k, print the k largest elements in ascending order of their final heap contents. This is a pure heap-usage readiness check for Java PriorityQueue and C++ priority_queue patterns.
outputFormat: Print the k largest elements in ascending order
intendedApproachSummary: Maintain a min-heap of size k and replace its top whenever a larger value arrives.
wrongApproachHints: Full sorting works but does not teach the heap pattern we want here.
Use a min-heap when keeping the top k largest values.
hints: Keep only k elements in the heap.
Sort the final heap contents before printing if needed.

functionContract.javaSignature: public int[] kLargestElements(int[] nums, int k)
